modules.summary: Sets up and runs the Express application server for the URL shortener. Handles configuration loading, middleware setup, error handling, route mounting, and server initialization on startup.

Manages the core URL shortening functionality: generates short codes and aliases, stores links in memory, applies business logic (validation, expiration, visit tracking), and exposes the shortener through HTTP routes.

project.name: Express URL Shortener
project.purpose: A TypeScript-based URL shortening service built with Express that generates short codes and aliases for URLs, stores them in memory, tracks visits, and exposes the functionality through HTTP routes.
project.architecture: The server starts at src/server.ts and initializes an Express app configured in src/app.ts. The app mounts links routes from src/links/links.routes.ts, which expose HTTP endpoints. These routes delegate to src/links/links.service.ts, which applies business logic like validation and expiration. The service uses src/links/links.store.ts to read and write links from in-memory storage. At the foundation, src/links/link.ts defines the link data model, src/links/code-generator.ts generates short codes, src/config.ts loads environment configuration, and src/errors.ts defines error types. Each layer depends only on layers below it, creating a clean separation from data models and utilities up through storage and service logic to HTTP routes and finally server initialization.
keyConcepts: Layered architecture with separation of concerns
